title: SOFR Daily Rate — Week of April 20–24, 2026
summary: SOFR settled at 3.66% on April 24, 2026, up 1 bp from the prior day and 3 bps above the April 20 reading of 3.63%, reflecting a modest upward drift in overnight secured funding costs over the observation week.
key_points: SOFR closed at 3.66% on April 24, 2026 (latest observation)
Prior day SOFR was 3.65% on April 23, 2026
Absolute change from April 23 to April 24: +1 bp
SOFR is the Secured Overnight Financing Rate, used as the primary benchmark for short-term lending markets and derivatives pricing
why_it_matters: SOFR is the dominant reference rate for trillions of dollars in floating-rate contracts, repo markets, and short-term funding. Even small daily moves signal shifting conditions in the overnight banking system and influence the effective cost of leverage across markets.
macro_context: Remove the specific Fed funds target claim (4.25–4.50%). The source only provides SOFR observations and does not include any Fed funds rate reference. A corrected version would read: 'A drifting upward in SOFR suggests persistent tightness in overnight funding. SOFR typically trades close to the effective Fed funds rate, making it a barometer of banking system liquidity conditions.'
market_structure_context: SOFR is compiled from overnight Treasury general collateral repo transactions cleared through the Fixed Income Clearing Corporation. It is the foundational rate for the Fed's ongoing balance sheet normalization (QT) framework and serves as the fallback rate referenced in SOFR-linked derivatives and loan agreements.
